suggested_issue_title: pyproject.toml build-backend "setuptools.backends.legacy:build" does not exist; package is not published on PyPI as aspose-html-foss
suggested_issue_body:
## Summary

Building this repository's own source with the standard Python packaging toolchain fails, and no distribution named `aspose-html-foss` is published on PyPI.

## Environment

- Repository: aspose-html-foss/Aspose.HTML-FOSS-for-Python
- Revision: `bf0f1e7a6d29ca9e14de576fe3ff1aa49ddbaf11` (default branch `main`)
- Tool: pip (any standard version); Python 3.10+

## Steps to reproduce

1. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://pypi.org/pypi/aspose-html-foss/json`
2. Clone the repository at the revision above and run: `pip install --target <dir> .`

## Actual result

1. Returns `404` - no distribution named `aspose-html-foss` exists on PyPI.
2. Fails during the build with:

   ```
   pip._vendor.pyproject_hooks._impl.BackendUnavailable: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'setuptools.backends'
   ```

## Root cause

`pyproject.toml` line 3 declares:

```toml
build-backend = "setuptools.backends.legacy:build"
```

`setuptools.backends.legacy` is not a module any released version of `setuptools` ships. The corresponding entry point for a `setuptools`-based build is `setuptools.build_meta`. Because of this declaration, `pip install .` fails for any caller building this exact source, not only in one particular environment.

## Additional note

This repository's own `README.md`, as of this revision, does not document `pip install aspose-html-foss` - it documents cloning the repository and adding `src/` to `PYTHONPATH` directly, which does work. Filing this in case a PyPI-published, `pip install`-able distribution is intended to be a supported install path.
